entry.title: Build your own (19 Oct 2026): Re-test, 19 October 2026: 6 of 6 tests, 82.0 Hz bit-exact. The beginner path re-run from an empty folder on 19 Oct 2026 (Linux x86_64, Python 3.11.2, 2 CPUs) with the pinned packages. No page fixes were needed. Pins: unchanged; checked against PyPI on 19 Oct 2026 (latest: Brian2 2.10.1, numpy 2.5.4, pandas 3.0.6, mujoco 3.16.0; our pins stay at 2.9.0, 2.3.5, 2.3.3 and 3.9.0), and installed cleanly in the re-test of 19 Oct; next re-test due 2 Nov 2026. On 19 Oct 2026 the short requirements.txt command picked 5 newer helper packages than our exact lock (iniconfig 2.3.0 → 2.3.1, MarkupSafe 3.0.3 → 3.0.4, pluggy 1.6.0 → 1.7.0, pytz 2026.4 → 2026.5, tzdata 2026.4 → 2026.5); the six main packages are pinned and did not change. Use requirements.lock to get exactly our environment. Quick look (200 ms trials), run on 19 Oct 2026 in 1.7 min: sugar 80.0 Hz → extend proboscis; shuffled wiring 0.0 Hz → stay still. Shorter trials are noisier than the full run. The quick-look command is now labelled tested.

In the body (19 Oct 2026, our own test, pre-registered, one run): 19 Oct: walked in the body, the one matched scrambled brain with a small steering signal changed the fly's heading by about 1.4 degrees away from the shadow compared with no brain input, under our 10-degree turn rule; the real brain, with the same input, turned it away by about 16.8 degrees (one run each). This body run turns the brain's firing rates into steering through our own hand-made mapping; it is not a separate test of the wiring. The 30 spikes/s closing is unchanged.

171 catalogue entries (19 Oct 2026): 10 new: malecns-cube (A; ledger: no difference), qedsdl-endpoint (A; mixed), flybrain-llm-substrate (A; worse), 3dfly (B), flywirelm (B), chatflypt (B), fastfly (B), bsc-vfb (n/a), and two U rows, origozero-fruit-fly (OrigoZero "Fruit Fly"; the page says the whole MaleCNS v1.0 connectome runs as spiking neurons on the GPU and drives a fly in an arena; no code linked) and flyproject-connectome-explorer (flyproject.io; the page calls itself "a real fruit fly brain, one circuit at a time"; no repository, licence or author): page responds, checked 19 Oct 2026; not loaded in a browser by us. A re-host of Lulzx/fly-brain is counted under fly-brain-lulzx.

Controls ledger (19 Oct 2026): 3 new rows (a trainable network on a 256-node MaleCNS v1.0 subgraph estimates how far a Rubik's cube state is from solved; a degree-preserving rewired graph (test error 0.338) and a parameter-matched MLP (0.325) do as well as the real wiring (0.351), 3 seeds; the FlyWire v783 wiring from projection neurons to Kenyon cells is the fixed input layer of a novelty detector for simulated Raman spectra (a materials-lab task); AUROC real 0.9505, degree-preserving shuffle 0.9505, random wiring 0.9391 (20 seeds); a MaleCNS v1.0 network runs flies in an evolving foraging economy; weight-permuted wiring ends with more energy than the real wiring on all 3 seeds (742.93 vs 360.27 mean energy), and zeroed weights starve), now 65 studies, 56 with a wiring null: helps 25, no difference 12, worse 5, mixed 12, not yet scored 2. Activity numbers now say what they count (display only); for the gain-matched looming arm the whole-brain ratio 0.9864 is shown with the count outside the stimulated input, 0.98. Scoring unchanged.

Corrections (19 Oct 2026): fly67's author field is "Ruben Gexhaw (GitHub: gexhaw, formerly znatgost)" and chessfly's "Ruben Nugmanov (GitHub: gexhaw, formerly znatgost)", each from its repository's LICENSE; fly67's size is about 33 MB (measured on our 18 Oct 2026 load; the README says 31-33 MB gzipped). Odyssey-3 claim: No method, code or write-up was published as of 19 Oct 2026.

Tracking (19 Oct 2026): repositories of 15 of the 23 verdict rows re-checked, none with new code since grading; 56 of 56 videos available; fruitfly.live still has a TLS certificate error; FlyDoom's repository still answers "not found".

New report: Twentieth check (19 Oct 2026), with the beginner re-test from an empty folder, the body walk of one strengthened scrambled brain, new entries and ledger rows, what each activity number counts, corrections, tracking and limits.

Scrambled brains at 30 spikes/s, strengthened (18 Oct 2026, our own test, pre-registered, brain only): 18 Oct: we then strengthened the connections inside scrambled brains (not the input) until their neurons outside the stimulated input fired about as many spikes as in the real brain (within 30%; same input, one 1-second trial each). On the left side, 2 scrambled brains matched this way, and neither sent a turn command. On the right side, 2 scrambled brains matched this way, and neither sent a turn command. Matching the number of spikes does not match the pattern: 1,152 to 2,228 neurons fired in the matched scrambled brains, against 379 (left) and 432 (right) in the real brain. 1 of the matched scrambled brains sent small steering signals, which we did not walk in the body. As at 80 spikes/s, none of the scrambled brains we ran at 30 spikes/s sent a turn command, including those strengthened to about the real brain's activity outside the input.

Browser: Correction, 18 Oct: our 17 Oct check loaded fly67's old address, which answered 'not found'; the project now lives at gexhaw.github.io/fly67/. At that address it ran on 18 Oct. Fly Worker, re-checked 18 Oct: ran by our check's rule (two workers and WebAssembly started, and text on the page changed); our screenshots showed only the top of the page, so we did not see the fly itself. Latest no-GPU browser check: 3 of 6 ran (17 Oct; fly67 and Fly Worker re-checked 18 Oct). 3 Oct: 3 of 6. Checked in headless Chromium 154 on a Linux server without a GPU, 18 Oct 2026. Shows whether the page loads, downloads its brain data and keeps computing; it is not a play test. Safari, Firefox, phones and GPU machines were not tested.

161 catalogue entries (18 Oct 2026): 5 new: flysnake (A; a MaleCNS v1.0 network plays Snake through a trained readout; on 100 held-out games the real wiring scored 20.03 food per game, a rewired graph with its own trained readout 3.63, and a hand-written rule 21.52), flywire-snn-stdp (A; ledger: mixed), fruitfly-terraria-moonlord (B), biogrid (B) and the U verdict row odyssey3-fly-world-model-claim. 18 other leads excluded (no committed result file or wiring comparison we could read, or a copy of another lead).

New verdict row, odyssey3-fly-world-model-claim (U): Odyssey said on X on 17 Oct 2026 that it placed "the fruit fly brain" inside its Odyssey-3 world model. No method, code or write-up was published as of 18 Oct 2026, so the claim cannot be checked. What would settle it: a write-up or code that names the fly brain model, how its outputs drive the flight and how the world model feeds it input.

Controls ledger (18 Oct 2026): 2 new rows (flysnake helps, its no-brain baseline not beaten; flywire-snn-stdp mixed), now 62 studies, 53 with a wiring null: helps 25, no difference 11, worse 4, mixed 11, not yet scored 2. A caveat marker for reading only on 8 rows; scoring and counts unchanged. byo-flygym-loom is not re-scored; the strengthened 30 spikes/s trials are in its note.

Tracking (18 Oct 2026): repositories of 15 of the 23 verdict rows re-checked, none with new code since grading; 56 of 56 videos available; fly67 and chessfly answer at their gexhaw addresses; fruitfly.live still has a TLS certificate error; FlyDoom's repository still answers "not found".

New report: Nineteenth check (18 Oct 2026), with the strengthened scrambled brains at 30 spikes/s and their checks, the fly67 correction and Fly Worker re-check, new entries and ledger rows, the caveat marker, the Odyssey-3 verdict row, tracking and limits.

Scrambled brains at 30 spikes/s (17 Oct 2026, our own test, pre-registered, brain only): 17 Oct: at 30 spikes/s, the weakest tested input at which the real brain's turn command appeared, we also ran 2 scrambled brains per side (each neuron keeps its number of connections; one 1-second trial each, with the same trial seed as the real-wiring body runs). On the left side, neither scrambled brain sent a turn command, and their steering signals were identical to having no brain, so in the body they walk like the no-brain fly (the real wiring turned it about 11 deg). On the right side, neither scrambled brain sent a turn command, and their steering signals were identical to having no brain, so in the body they walk like the no-brain fly (the real wiring turned it about 17 deg). As at 80 spikes/s, none of the scrambled brains we ran produced the turn; at 30 spikes/s we did not turn their activity up to match the real brain. The scrambled brains were not matched for overall activity: they fired 48% (left) and 44% (right) as many spikes as the real brain at this strength. Most of those spikes were the stimulated input neurons themselves; outside the input, the scrambled brains fired about 1% as many spikes as the real brain. These body runs turn the brain's firing rates into steering through our own hand-made mapping, so they show the brain result in degrees; they are not a separate test of the wiring. We ran scrambled brains at 30 and 80 spikes/s, not at 20, 40 or 60.

Relay update under the 13 Oct headline, which stays (17 Oct 2026; a count from the map, not a new trial): "The two sides disagree: on one side silencing the relays lowered the turn neuron's rate more than matched activity elsewhere, on the other it did not. We do not draw a conclusion." We also looked for a stricter control: other active inputs that excite the turn neuron with a similar firing rate and a similar number of connections onto it. In this model there are none for any of the active relay neurons on either side (count of 15 Oct: the busiest relay, PVLP141, fires about 100 spikes/s; no other such input fires above 43), so that stricter test cannot be built here.

Browser re-check of the six demos of 3 Oct: Re-checked 17 Oct in the same no-GPU browser: 1 of 6 ran (3 Oct: 3 of 6). Fly Worker: loaded, but showed no activity (3 Oct: ran). fly67: did not load (3 Oct: ran). Checked in headless Chromium 154 on a Linux server without a GPU, 17 Oct 2026. Shows whether the page loads, downloads its brain data and keeps computing; it is not a play test. Safari, Firefox, phones and GPU machines were not tested.

156 catalogue entries (17 Oct 2026): 4 new: flycraft-hexapod (A; in the author's test the real nerve-cord graph moved the hexapod 0.85 mm forward in 8 s, fully rewired graphs 3.5 mm backward, and a time-shuffled real signal 0.72 mm; the author's results file is marked pending the author's own review, and the paper's acceptance is the author's statement only), fly-connectome-reservoir (B; no wiring control on its game; its separate reservoir test scores real wiring 100%, target-permuted wiring 83.9% and no connections 50% (3 seeds); a raw-stimulus readout also reaches 100%), virtual-fly-brain-ppo (D) and fruit-fly-connectome-explorer (n/a). Nine other leads excluded (no committed result file or wiring comparison in code).

Controls ledger (17 Oct 2026): 2 new rows (flycraft-hexapod helps; fly-connectome-reservoir helps, its no-brain baseline not beaten), now 60 studies, 51 with a wiring null: helps 24, no difference 11, worse 4, mixed 10, not yet scored 2. byo-flygym-loom is not re-scored; the 30 spikes/s trials are in its note.

Tracking (17 Oct 2026): roblox-fly-avatar-claim stays U (Referee check: no builder named in the NiftRex video description or on the Roblox profile (17 Oct).); repositories of 15 of the 22 verdict rows re-checked, none with new code since grading; 56 of 56 videos available; fruitfly.live still has a TLS certificate error; FlyDoom is still gone.
